policy_title: Revitalise High Streets and Tackle Street Scars/Fly Tipping
stated: The Conservative Party will revitalise high streets by changing planning laws to support local market days and regenerate shopping centres. They will also make industry pay for removing chewing-gum, raise fines for utility firms' 'street scars', and make fly tipping an offence carrying penalty points against driving licences.

source.quote: Give our high streets a new lease of life and restore pride in place. We will change planning laws to support places to bring back local market days and regenerate defunct shopping centres. ...We will make fly tipping an offence that carries penalty points against your driving licence.

bearing_set.reason: Making fly tipping a penalty-point offence and raising fines for utility street scars are enforcement/deterrence measures directly targeting antisocial behaviour and crime, earning a real verdict on whether streets are safer and justice works.

Both the fly tipping crackdown and the industry levy for chewing-gum removal directly address urban environmental cleanliness and waste contamination, earning a real verdict on whether the local environment is liveable.

Changing planning law to enable local market days and regenerate shopping centres directly targets local business activity, firm-level opportunity, and economic dynamism — concrete O13 mechanisms for real living-standards effects.

Local market days and vibrant high streets are well-evidenced community-gathering infrastructure; the planning changes are designed to strengthen civic participation and social trust, core O15 indicators.

membership_note: Policy bundles four distinct measures; each maps to a separate fundamental via a concrete mechanism. No tax or public-finance implications material enough to engage O11/O12 (fines/industry levies are modest and indirect). O10 (liberty) considered for penalty-points enforcement but standard criminal-law penalties do not reach the coercive/surveillance threshold for a non-negligible O10 bearing.
